subject.title: [Security] Arbitrary file read via symlink dereferencing in diagnostics exporter

question: Does the diagnostics exporter currently consume an attacker-controlled filesystem entry in a way that can place an out-of-boundary file into an approved support bundle?
rationale: The public report alleges a serious boundary violation but does not demonstrate the exporter entry point, trust prerequisites, resulting archive contents, or whether the named secret-file module participates in the path.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Ask the reporter for a minimal directory layout, invocation, archive listing, tested SHA or release, and redacted proof through the repository security channel before selecting a fix.

options.title: Close as unsupported
options.body: Close only if source inspection proves the exporter never traverses attacker-controlled directories and the reporter cannot provide a concrete counterexample.

recommendation.title: Request private reproduction
recommendation.body: Ask the reporter for a minimal directory layout, invocation, archive listing, tested SHA or release, and redacted proof through the repository security channel before selecting a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available repository-policy routing candidate for deciding whether the allegation crosses a supported security boundary.
